## 1. Objective

One paragraph: the scope this plan governs, and what it does not govern.

---

## 2. Scope

In scope, then a table of exclusions **with the reason for each**. Close with the default-exclusion
rule: anything not specifically included is excluded. In manual testing that bounds effort; with an
agent authoring tests it also bounds invention.

## 4. Testing approach

Tiers (risk/speed axis), and **where each rule is enforced** — write time, merge time, or CI. That
placement decides whether a violation can reach review at all.

### 4.1 Verification layers

Layer is the stack-depth axis, independent of tier. State which of `ui` / `api` / `service` / `db`
are reachable **for this target**, and mark unreachable ones as unreachable-by-access rather than
descoped. Requirements record this in `layers: [...]`; `coverage-computed.json` reports
`layers.byLayer` and `layers.crossLayer`.

Backend and cross-layer coverage model:
`docs/backend-testing-coverage.md`.

---

## 5. Test environments and mutation policy

Environment × data class × allowed operations × approval. The mutation boundary is the safety-critical
column: it decides what an agent is permitted to do.

---

## 6. Test data strategy

Roll up, do not restate: module contexts own per-module lifecycle, `project-context.md` owns
per-environment data class. State here what is permanently forbidden (credentials, PII, payment data,
production records) and what a mutating requirement must satisfy before leaving `draft` — synthetic
only, isolation key, failure-safe cleanup, cleanup failure is a test failure, declared before BUILD.

---

## 7. Application flow documents

A requirement touching one module needs a module context. A requirement whose steps are owned by
different modules needs a flow context first — from
`docs/application-intelligence/_template/flow-context.md` — or the agent invents the seams between
them.

---

## 8. Phases

One heading per phase with an explicit status. For each: entry criteria, exit criteria, and the
decision id blocking it. A phase with no exit criterion never ends.

---

## 9. Definition of done for one requirement

A table of criteria and **what checks each one**. Prefer machine-checked rows; mark anything
human-judged as such. Define coverage as _every active requirement maps to exactly one passing test_
rather than a line or branch percentage.

---

## 10. Provenance and approval

Who or what did each step, and where the record lives: context, draft, **approval** (the human gate),
authoring, gate verdict, execution. Name the gaps — a verdict log with no actor field cannot attribute
a decision to the agent and policy version that produced it.

---

## 11. Policy and engine versioning

The agents and rules are inputs to the output; changing them changes what gets authored. List what is
pinned and what proves it. Rules graded by model judgment need a fixture corpus with recorded expected
verdicts, re-run on any model, prompt, or engine change.

---

## 12. Authority boundaries

What the agent may never do, regardless of instruction. At minimum: invent an application fact, build
from a non-active requirement, write a credential literal, mutate beyond approved operations, redefine
an existing requirement id, or exceed the gate repair limit without escalating.

---

## 13. Deliverables

Generated artifacts and what produces each. If a person maintains a row here by hand, it will drift —
generate it or delete it.

---

## 14. Suspension, resumption, and exit criteria

Suspension triggers, resumption conditions, and phase exit criteria. Resumption must require fixing
the cause, never loosening the assertion. Avoid "all test cases executed" — it is not falsifiable.

---

## 15. Open decisions

`D<n>` · decision · owner · what it blocks. In an agentic loop an unanswered decision is a stall, so
it belongs in the plan as a first-class blocker.

---

## 16. Risks

Risk · likelihood · impact · response. Mark unmitigated risks as unmitigated; a response column with
no gaps in it is not being honest.

---

## 17. Cadence

What runs per PR, per requirement, and on a schedule. Prefer cycle time per requirement over dated
waterfall phases.

---

## 18. Revision history

Tracked in git. `git log --follow docs/test-automation-plan.md` is the authoritative history; a
hand-maintained table is a second copy that drifts.
